page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 16 virtual CPUs utilizing a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU. Acceleration is driven by three NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The hardware profile presents distinct architectural tradeoffs. While the inclusion of three NVIDIA L4 GPUs offers substantial parallel processing capabilities and 72 GB of VRAM, the CPU resources are provisioned on a shared allocation model, which may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-core CPU workloads. Additionally, the absence of local storage requires users to attach external block storage for operating systems and data persistence. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance maximizes GPU and memory density relative to its CPU allocation, making it a specialized option for workloads that are heavily GPU-bound rather than CPU-bound.

Given the hardware configuration, this server is designed for workloads that leverage multi-GPU acceleration and large system memory footprints. Suitable workloads include machine learning inference, medium-scale AI model training, video transcoding, and parallel data processing pipelines that offload execution to the NVIDIA Ada Lovelace GPUs while requiring substantial system memory for data staging.
